description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of various fine-tuning methods on the GLUE benchmark, comparing two sizes of the RoBERTa model — “base” (blue bars) and “large” (orange bars) — across multiple adaptation techniques. The vertical axis, labeled “GLUE Performance,” ranges from approximately 86 to 88, with tick marks at 86, 87, and 88, indicating a narrow but meaningful performance spread. The horizontal axis lists fine-tuning methods: “LoRA,” “BitFit,” “S₁-model,” “S₄-model,” and “S₅-model,” with some method labels partially cut off on the left. For each method, two adjacent bars show the performance of the base and large models. Notably, the “large” model consistently outperforms the “base” model across all methods. The “S₅-model” achieves the highest performance, with the large variant approaching 88.5, while the “BitFit” method shows the lowest performance, especially for the base model, which dips below 86.5. The legend in the upper left clearly distinguishes the two model sizes by color, and the bars are grouped by method, enabling direct comparison between model sizes within each technique. The chart visually emphasizes that model size and fine-tuning strategy both significantly impact downstream task performance.
